steps.message:
# Close the Alameda store

The Alameda store closes today (2026-09-14). Its stock is the `alameda` warehouse of the `inventory` service, which also holds the item records and the stock of the other stores. Its customer tickets are in the `tickets` service, team `store-alameda`. The closure plan (where each item goes, the items that cannot travel, the receiving capacity of each store), the hazardous goods permits and the customer responses for the closure are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `inventory` and `docs` MCP servers.

Carry out the closure exactly as the current closure plan says, under the permits in force today. The docs service also holds superseded revisions; follow only the current ones.

- Stock: empty `alameda` by moving or writing off every unit as the plan says, with `adjust_stock` under the plan's reference. Book nothing else and leave all other stock as it is. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.
- Customer tickets: add exactly one comment to each ticket the plan covers, with the matching customer response as written in the docs (the store name filled in where the response has one), and set its status as the plan says. Leave every other ticket unchanged.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"closure-plan-alameda\",\"title\":\"Closure plan: Alameda store\",\"tags\":[\"closure\",\"stores\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-01\",\"body\":\"# Closure plan: Alameda store\\n\\nRevision 2026-09, in force since 2026-09-01. Replaces revision 2026-07.\\n\\nThe Alameda store (warehouse `alameda` in inventory) closes on 2026-09-14. Every unit it holds leaves it that day, and its open customer tickets are answered.\\n\\n## Stock\\n\\nBook every movement with `adjust_stock` under the reference `CLOSURE-ALM-0914`. A move to a destination is a `transfer` of minus the units in `alameda` and a `transfer` of plus the units at the destination. A write-off is a `damage` of minus the units in `alameda`.\\n\\nTake the items that `alameda` holds in sku order, lowest first, and handle each one by the first rule that applies:\\n\\n1. Discontinued items (the item's `discontinued` flag in inventory): every unit goes to `returns`, the return center.\\n2. Items that cannot travel: the `plants` category. Every unit is written off.\\n3. Every other item goes to the receiving stores of its category, in the order listed below. Each store in turn takes as many units as its remaining receiving capacity allows; the units no store takes go to `returns`.\\n\\nA receiving store takes an item only if it carries it: the item has a stock record for that store in inventory, even one at 0. For the `chemicals` category, a store takes the item only if its hazardous goods permit is in force on the day of the move (see the hazardous goods permits).\\n\\n## Receiving stores by category\\n\\n- tools: bellavista, costanera\\n- paint: costanera, dunas\\n- garden: dunas, bellavista\\n- chemicals: dunas, costanera, bellavista\\n\\n## Receiving capacity\\n\\nThe free shelf capacity each receiving store has for this closure, in units, shared by every item it takes. `returns` has no limit.\\n\\n- bellavista: 60\\n- costanera: 45\\n- dunas: 30\\n\\n## Customer tickets\\n\\nEvery open ticket of team `store-alameda` labeled `customer` gets one comment with the matching response from the store closure customer responses, and a new status.\\n\\n- Pickup orders (label `pickup`): the order moves to the store that received the most units of its item in this closure; on a tie, the one listed first for the item's category. It moves only if that store received at least the order quantity. Comment `pickup-moved` with that store, status `pending`. Otherwise, or when no store received the item, comment `pickup-cancelled`, status `closed`.\\n- Workshop bookings (label `workshop`): comment `workshop`, status `closed`.\\n- Other questions (label `inquiry`): they move to the bellavista store. Comment `inquiry` with that store, status `pending`.\\n\\nLeave internal tickets and the tickets of other teams as they are.\\n\"}"}

steps.message:
The Alameda closure is done. The `alameda` warehouse is at 0 and the 12 open customer tickets have their comments and new statuses. `/app/STATUS.json` says "success". I read the `adjust_stock` results (each showed `alameda` at 0) but didn't re-query inventory afterwards.

**Stock** (all booked under `CLOSURE-ALM-0914`, following the current plan revision 2026-09)
- **Chemicals:** only costanera's permit covers 2026-09-14. Dunas' expired on 2026-08-31 and bellavista's starts on 2026-10-01.
- **Pool chlorine:** all 9 units went to costanera.
- **Weed killer:** costanera took 2, the rest of its capacity, and the other 6 went to `returns`.
- **Plants:** the lavender pots (16) and olive trees (3) were written off.
- **Discontinued:** the 6 grey primer went to `returns`.
- **Tape measures:** all 12 went to `returns`, because bellavista and costanera had no capacity left.
- **Everything else:** moved to the receiving stores in the plan's order.

**Tickets**
- **Pickups moved, status `pending`:**
  - 2201 to bellavista
  - 2208 to costanera
  - 2214 to dunas
  - 2216 to bellavista
- **Pickups cancelled, status `closed`:**
  - 2203 (lavender)
  - 2210 (primer)
  - 2217 (weed killer, since costanera received only 2 of the 3 ordered)
  - 2220 (tape measures)
- **Workshop bookings, status `closed`:** 2206 and 2218.
- **Inquiries, status `pending`:** 2212 and 2222 went to bellavista.

I left alone ticket 2204 (already `pending`), ticket 2209 (already `resolved`) and the two internal tickets.
